arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import statistics

# Data points (in millions of foreign currency units)
belgian_francs = [12060, 2245, 16408, 13327]
canadian_dollars = [10371, 10724, 11176, 10806]

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(belgian_francs)
mean_x = statistics.mean(belgian_francs)
mean_y = statistics.mean(canadian_dollars)

# Calculate covariance
covariance = sum((belgian_francs[i] - mean_x) * (canadian_dollars[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n)) / (n - 1)

# Calculate standard deviations (sample)
std_x = statistics.stdev(belgian_francs)
std_y = statistics.stdev(canadian_dollars)

# Pearson correlation
pearson_corr = covariance / (std_x * std_y)

print(f'Belgian Francs: {belgian_francs}')
print(f'Canadian Dollars: {canadian_dollars}')
print(f'Mean Belgian Francs: {mean_x}')
print(f'Mean Canadian Dollars: {mean_y}')
print(f'Std Belgian Francs: {std_x}')
print(f'Std Canadian Dollars: {std_y}')
print(f'Pearson Correlation: {pearson_corr}')
print(f'Rounded to 4 decimal places: {round(pearson_corr, 4)}')
"

import statistics

# Using most current/revised values from the bulletins
# Dec 1975: from March bulletin (only source)
# Mar 1976: from April bulletin (most recent revision - 2246)
# June 1976: from May bulletin (most recent revision - 11175)
# Sept 1976: from May bulletin (only source)

belgian_francs = [12060, 2246, 16408, 13327]
canadian_dollars = [10371, 10724, 11175, 10806]

print('Data points:')
for i, (bf, cd) in enumerate(zip(belgian_francs, canadian_dollars)):
    print(f'  Point {i+1}: BF={bf}, CD={cd}')

# Manual calculation to verify
n = len(belgian_francs)
mean_x = sum(belgian_francs) / n
mean_y = sum(canadian_dollars) / n

print(f'\\nMeans: BF={mean_x}, CD={mean_y}')

# Covariance (sample)
numerator = sum((bf - mean_x) * (cd - mean_y) for bf, cd in zip(belgian_francs, canadian_dollars))
covariance = numerator / (n - 1)

# Standard deviations (sample)
var_x = sum((bf - mean_x)**2 for bf in belgian_francs) / (n - 1)
var_y = sum((cd - mean_y)**2 for cd in canadian_dollars) / (n - 1)
std_x = var_x ** 0.5
std_y = var_y ** 0.5

print(f'Std dev: BF={std_x}, CD={std_y}')
print(f'Covariance: {covariance}')

pearson = covariance / (std_x * std_y)
print(f'\\nPearson correlation: {pearson}')
print(f'Rounded: {round(pearson, 4)}')"
